items.title: Above every element there is a binary tree of arbitrary finite height
items.author: Silvia Barbina; Enrique Casanovas
items.work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 841-846: for an HF-ordering of an infinite Steiner triple system, every element a and every finite n, there is a binary tree of height n above a whose nodes increase along the extension relation. The proof (source lines 847-859) builds the tree by recursion on the height, and the step uses the earlier structural fact that below a product decomposition there are two elements above any prescribed bound, which is what makes the two branches available at every node; the two ordering properties are then read off the recursive choice. The statement records the existence of the tree and neither the recursion nor the structural input at each node.
